column6: Explain tool calling as the model asking for an action, not taking it.
column11:
Part 1: Tool Calling and MCP
• Explain how missing context and model training contribute to hallucinated answers.
• Distinguish problems solved with supplied context from those requiring live external data.
• Use an LLM to extract structured inputs from natural-language requests.
• Design the three-layer tool-calling flow: LLM, backend execution environment, and deterministic tool.

Part 2: The Road to MCP
• Decide when a tool is needed, which tool to select, and when clarification is necessary.
• Describe tools using names, descriptions, parameter types, and structured schemas.
• Separate the model’s tool-call decision from the backend’s execution responsibility.
• Explain how MCP standardizes tool discovery and communication, and when a direct integration is sufficient.

• Diagnose whether a failure comes from missing knowledge, outdated information, scale, or model behavior.

column6: Prepare a small clean dataset in Python and explain what clean means for it.

• Clean and normalize data, remove duplicates, redact sensitive information, and prevent training–evaluation leakage.
• Create consistent instruction-input-output or conversation examples with accurate annotations.
• Improve dataset diversity and edge-case coverage, validate quality, and iterate based on model failures.

column6: Run an eval with a written rubric, and judge the judge: show one case where the LLM grader was wrong.

• Compare public benchmarks, automated metrics, LLM judges, and human evaluation.
• Validate automated judgments against human reviews and use clear rubrics or A/B comparisons.
• Use evaluation failures to improve prompts, training data, and model behavior continuously.
